problem: Given that the expression $2\sqrt{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ can be written as $R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-ϕ)$ with $0<ϕ<\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $R>0$, what is the value of $ϕ?$

feedback.problem: Given that the expression $2\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+8\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)$ can be written as $R\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x-ϕ)$ with $0<ϕ<\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $R>0$, what is the value of $ϕ?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The difference formula for cosine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+8\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+8\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)=(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=8 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=2\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{2}{8} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{1}{4} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{1}{4}).\end{aligned}
$$
